text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Spike in GPU OOMs during prefill observed in cluster us-east1. Metric: prefill_container_restart_count increased by 400% in 4m. Auto-page sent to oncall. thread 1765432386

oncall-aaron: Acknowledged. Eng-runtime and eng-sre, please triage. Any correlation with the long-context traffic surge?

sasha: I'm seeing repeated container exits with exit code 137. Prefill allocator tries to reserve very large KV caches for a few requests. Sample trace: 
```
[2026-03-02T22:10:12Z] prefill: incoming tokens=1_180_000
[2026-03-02T22:10:12Z] allocator: reserve_kv 1180000 -> bytes=952MiB
[2026-03-02T22:10:12Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc(...) -> ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-02T22:10:12Z] process: killed with SIGKILL (OOM)
```

maya: Affected pool: inference-us-east1-gpu-pool-2 (A100s). 9 pods restarted across 2 nodes since 22:06. Node memory pressure high and we saw kubelet evict thresholds hit.

eng-runtime-lead: Hypothesis: malicious/accidental very long-context requests circumventing prefix limits. We should enable a short-term safe-guard: trim prefill to 65k tokens or reject >200k tokens with 413. Which should we do first?

oncall-aaron: Fastest mitigation path: flip runtime trim flag for the impacted model tag and simultaneously apply a soft rate-limit on >200k requests. Eng-sre, can you isolate noisy nodes to stop churn?

eng-sre-lina: Starting node isolation. I'll cordon node-21 and node-22 and migrate critical traffic. Also adding a temporary BPF policy to throttle extremely large allocations.

eng-runtime-lead: I'll push runtime-prefill trim for the model family rw/gptx-30b in us-east region. Deploy-bot please run the config patch.

deploy-bot: patch submitted: PATCH /v1/configs/rw/gptx-30b {"prefill.max_tokens_trim": "65536", "prefill.reject_over": "200000"}  rollout id 20260302-003  start

sasha: Captured container core dump from one restart and uploaded to s3 for diagnostics: s3://redwood-incidents/1765432386/coredump-1.tar.gz

support-ivy: Drafting status page message. Need to confirm region and mitigation text before posting.

oncall-aaron: Quick customer triage: cs-raj, any paying customers showing elevated 5xx rates? If so, ask them to route traffic to eu-west1 temporarily.

customer-success-raj: Notified two enterprise customers on ongoing calls. AcmeChat routing to eu-west1 and saw immediate drop in errors. They requested an ETA for full fix.

eng-sre-lina: Node cordon/drain done for node-21. Evicted 5 pods; scheduler rescheduled to other pools. Memory pressure reduced. Also created an emergency alert to mute flapping alerts to reduce noise for oncall.

deploy-bot: rollout id 20260302-003 completed: 10/10 instances updated in us-east1 at 22:13:06Z.

eng-runtime-lead: After trim enabled, test with synthetic payload ~1.1M tokens: prefill trimmed to 65,536 tokens; allocation dropped from ~900MB -> ~88MB and no OOM on local canary. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-02T22:13:14Z] runtime: prefill_trim applied (requested=1_100_000, trimmed=65536)
[2026-03-02T22:13:14Z] allocator: allocate kv_cache bytes=92_000_000
[2026-03-02T22:13:14Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc succeeded
```

oncall-aaron: Good. Lina, monitor restart_rate and OOM metrics for 15m, then we determine if we can uncordon. Support, post short status.

eng-sre-lina: Monitoring: prefill_oom_rate fell from 1.1% to 0.03% in 6 minutes. Pod restart rate normalized. Uncordoning node-21 now.

support-ivy: Posted status update: "We detected elevated OOMs affecting long-context inference in us-east1. We applied a mitigation that trims excessively long prefill requests; service health is recovering. We'll follow up with an RCA and timeline for permanent fixes." :white_check_mark:

customer-success-raj: Customers updated. One large customer wants a configuration that allows larger context for dedicated capacity; we'll coordinate offline.

eng-runtime-lead: Follow-up actions: 1) Make prefill trimming a conservative default for rw/gptx family behind a canary; 2) Implement hard upper limit and informative 413 responses with guidance; 3) Improve allocator to do on-demand allocation instead of reserving full KV for pathological prefills; 4) Add alert for sudden allocation spikes and a metric prefill_alloc_bytes.p95.

oncall-aaron: Assigning owners and creating an incident ticket for the postmortem. Impact summary: brief service errors for long-context requests in us-east1; approx 0.8% of total requests in affected timeframe errored; no user data exposure.

sasha: Saved relevant logs, core dumps, and policy diffs to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/1765432386/artifacts.tgz

eng-sre-lina: I'll prepare postmortem draft with timeline, customer impact, and remediation plan. Also proposing we add a per-customer console alert for large-context usage spikes.

oncall-aaron: Pager closed - mitigation validated. Leaving incident open for follow-ups and RCA. Thanks team.

incidents-bot: Incident 1765432386 status updated: mitigated by oncall-aaron at 2026-03-02T22:30:30Z

oncall-aaron: Handoff to eng-runtime-lead for follow-up PRs and canary. If tests show regression we will reopen pager.

eng-runtime-lead: Acknowledged. Will own the follow-ups and schedule the allocator improvement in next sprint.

support-ivy: Logged all customer contacts and support cases in the incident ticket.

eng-sre-lina: Final note: consider adding an automated emergency config that temporarily trims prefill for model families when cluster memory pressure > 70% to avoid manual flips.

oncall-aaron: Noted. End of thread."
